children: Iraq is pushing ahead with a project to develop one of its largest gas fields as part of plans to stop gas flaring and become self-sufficient in gas production.
The Oil Ministry announced on Monday plans to increase gas production at the Nahr Bin Omar field to 300 million cubic feet per day (mcf/d).
It said in a statement that the project was discussed at a meeting of ministry officials, adding that it comprises two phases, each with a capacity of 150 mcf/d.

It noted that contract for investment, development and processing of gas in the Nahr Bin Omar field was referred to Halfaya Gas Company and was signed in January 2024 between the South Gas Company and Iraq’s Halfaya Gas Company.
“The project aims to produce 150 mcf/d in its first stage, with the possibility of adding 150 mcf/d in the second phase, to bring the total planned capacity to 300 million mcf/d.”
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
